verses.text: All the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings by the sea heard how the LORD had dried up the Jordan for the people of Israel until we had crossed. Their hearts melted with fear, and they lost all courage because of Israel.
At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make knives out of flint stone and circumcise the men of Israel again."
So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the men of Israel at a place called the Hill of Foreskins.
This is why he did it: all the men who left Egypt, all the fighting men, had died in the desert on the way.
All the men who came out of Egypt had been circumcised, but the boys born in the desert on the journey from Egypt had not.

The people of Israel had walked in the desert for forty years, until all the fighting men who left Egypt had died, because they did not obey the LORD. The LORD had sworn that they would not see the land he promised their ancestors to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
So Joshua circumcised their sons, whom God raised up in their place. They were not circumcised, because no one had done it on the journey.
After the whole nation was circumcised, they stayed in the camp until they were healed.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the shame of Egypt from you." So that place is called Gilgal to this day.
While the people of Israel camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, they celebrated the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month.
The day after the Passover, they ate food grown in the land: bread made without yeast and roasted grain.
The manna stopped the day after they ate food from the land. The people of Israel no longer had manna. That year they ate the crops of Canaan.
When Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him holding a sword. Joshua went to him and asked, "Are you on our side or on our enemies' side?"
He answered, "Neither. I have come as the commander of the LORD's army." Joshua bowed with his face to the ground and worshipped. He asked, "What does my lord want to say to his servant?"
The commander of the LORD's army said, "Take off your sandals, because the place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.
